<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level scope of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. In this PKGBUILD, the global scope contains only standard variable assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `options`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. All values are static or use simple parameter expansion (e.g., `${pkgver}`), with no command substitution, external downloads, or execution of untrusted code.

The `source` array references a Git repository with a specific tag (`v${pkgver}`), which is a common and acceptable practice for AUR packages. While the checksum is set to `'SKIP'`, this is not a concern for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` as no sources are downloaded or verified during this step. There is no evidence of malicious code execution during sourcing, such as `curl | bash`, `eval`, or data exfiltration attempts.

Thus, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe, as it will only parse metadata without triggering any dangerous operations.
</details>

No malicious top-level code; safe to parse.
